p01.why: Empty braces, = {}, and int() give each scalar and each array element zero, so the static_assert holds; there is no main, so the program is not run.

p02.why: Copying a value-less object into an unsigned char is not undefined under INIT-1, so the program returns 0.

p03.why: The constructor does not initialize y, so y has no value and reading it during constant evaluation is undefined and rejected.

p04.why: Each array element is default-initialized by the class default constructor, which uses the default member initializer 5, so the sum is 10; the spec does not say the implicit constructor may run in constant evaluation, but all programs of this kind assume it.

p05.why: The member inner is not in the initializer list, so it is default-initialized and its own default member initializer gives 7; 7 + 1 is 8.

p06.why: Default initialization runs the implicit constructor, which applies both default member initializers; 80 + 24 is 104.

p07.why: For a scalar the parentheses must hold exactly one expression.

p08.why: Declarators initialize left to right, so trace becomes 12 and a + b is 3.

p09.why: int x(); declares a function returning int, so decltype(x) is int().

p10.why: An array must not be initialized from another array.

p11.why: Elements without a value in the list get zero, and empty braces give all zeros.

p12.why: The implicit constructor of Derived default-initializes the base with Base() giving id 7 and applies extra = 1, so the sum is 8.

p13.why: The = form is copy-initialization and cannot use the explicit constructor.

p14.why: The constructor's words{} zeroes every element and g = {} zeroes the array, so main returns 0.

p15.why: new with no initializer default-initializes the Cell, which gets v = 5, and the storage is freed in the same evaluation.

p16.why: a[1] has no value; Clang and GCC reject the read in constant evaluation, while EDG 7.0 accepts it (Q-0013).

p17.why: v has no value, and the read during constant evaluation is rejected.

p18.why: x has no value, and the read during constant evaluation is rejected.

p19.why: Empty braces give an enumeration the value of 0, a pointer to member the null value, and nullptr_t the value nullptr.

p20.why: Parentheses and braces are direct forms, so the explicit constructor can be used; there is no main.

p21.why: The integer 1 does not convert to int*.

p22.why: x reads itself in its own initializer, where it has no value, so constant evaluation rejects the read.

p23.why: Copy and parenthesized initialization permit lossy conversions: 3.7 becomes 3, 300 becomes 44 in unsigned char, 2 becomes true.

p24.why: For a scalar the expression in parentheses must not be a braced list.

p25.why: An array without a bound initialized in parentheses gets the number of values, 3, as its bound.

p26.why: nullptr converts to bool only in direct initialization, and = is copy-initialization.

p27.why: Parenthesized array initialization fills given elements, zeroes the rest, and permits 1.5 to become 1.

p28.why: x gets a value by assignment before it is read.

p29.why: The type of the variable must be complete; the spec states this for = and parentheses, and I assume it also holds for braces.

p30.why: nullptr converts to bool in direct initialization with parentheses or braces and gives false.

p31.why: height has no default member initializer, so it has no value, and the read in constant evaluation is rejected.

p32.why: By INIT-1 the copy into unsigned char is not undefined, so CE-9 does not reject it; the spec gives no compiler evidence for this case in constant evaluation, so this is a guess.
